      subset: celmatch: at byte 27: list mixes int and string elements; a comparison across types cannot be decided, so whether this matches would depend on the order the entries are written in — use one type per list

== type-confusion/string-literal-vs-int-claim ==
! CEL=allow       SUBSET=deny        [numeric_id] assertion.big == 9007199254740993
      note: past float64's exact-integer range: JSON decoding has already lost the low bit
! CEL=allow       SUBSET=error       [numeric_id] assertion.fractional != 1
      subset: celmatch: claim is the non-integer number 1.5
! CEL=deny        SUBSET=error       [numeric_id] assertion.fractional == 1
      note: a fractional claim must not round into an int literal
      subset: celmatch: claim is the non-integer number 1.5
! CEL=deny        SUBSET=error       [numeric_id] assertion.huge == 1
      note: 1e300 does not fit an int64; the conversion must not wrap into a match
      subset: celmatch: claim is the non-integer number 1e+300
! CEL=allow       SUBSET=error       [numeric_id] assertion.repository_id != "123456"
      subset: celmatch: cannot compare int with string
! CEL=deny        SUBSET=error       [numeric_id] assertion.repository_id == "123456"
      note: mirror image: an IdP that really does send a number
      subset: celmatch: cannot compare int with string
  CEL=allow       SUBSET=allow       [numeric_id] assertion.repository_id == 123456
  CEL=allow       SUBSET=allow       [numeric_id] assertion.zero_point_zero == 74
      note: CEL has heterogeneous numeric equality: 74.0 == 74 is true
